title: What do we need to know about a new friend?
text:
Hi, I'm Pauline Lee and I'm 14 years old. I live in Singapore with my big family. I have a pet. It's a parrot. Her name is Coco. She can speak some Chinese! My favourite sport is tennis. I often play it with my friends after school. Do you want to be my friend?

Hi there! My name is Peter Brown. I'm 13 years old. I'm from London, in the UK. Now, I live in Beijing with my family. My favourite food is Beijing roast duck, and my favourite place is the Great Wall. I like music, and I play the guitar. Would you like to be my friend?

My name's Andre Kalu. I'm 13 years old. I'm from South Africa, but now I live in China. I live with my father, my mother, and my brother. We have a pet cat. His name is Toby. My favourite food is beef noodles. My favourite sport is basketball. I play basketball every weekend with my brother and my friends.

title: What do you like about your family?
text:
Hi, I'm Lily from Ireland. I love my big family. Here's a photo of us. I'm the one with the pink hat.

This is my dad, Fred. He's very handsome. He often plays tennis with me. My little brother, Sam, is on his knee. Sam is seven, and he really likes chess. This is my mum, Jane. She's beautiful and kind. She always reads with me at night. These are my grandparents, Jack and Sarah. They're my dad's parents. They have a dog. His name is Oscar.

My grandparents have three grandchildren: Sam, my cousin Lucy, and me. They often say I'm their favourite grandchild, but I think they say the same thing to all of us!

title: What fun things do you do at school?
text:

text:

title: Why is a tourist spot famous?
text:
Mount Taishan is in Shandong Province. It's one of the Five Great Mountains in China. Mount Taishan is famous for its wonderful views: springs, trees, birds, and flowers. When the sun rises or sets, the sky over the mountain turns orange, and the clouds turn pink and red. The top of the mountain is a wonderful place to enjoy the views. Lots of tourists climb Mount Taishan each year for the views.

I'm on Waikiki Beach now. It's in Hawaii. The beach has white sand and the sea is amazing! The water is usually blue and green, but when the sky turns pink, the water turns pink too. When the sun sets, the water turns yellow, orange, or purple.

There're also many interesting sea animals, such as sea lions, flying fish, and sea horses. I'm having a wonderful time here. Hope to see you soon!

title: Making New Friends at School
text:
Hello, boys and girls! Do you like to make new friends at school? Yes? Here's some of my advice.

First, don't be shy! Try to talk to all of your classmates. Smile and say, "Hello! What's your name?" If you didn't hear the name clearly, try, "Sorry, can you repeat that for me, please?" Then give your name and say, "Nice to meet you!" It's really as simple as that! It's important to get people's names right. If you get them wrong, they might feel sad!

Second, ask questions! Ask about school, sport, music, and more! As you listen, think of more questions to ask. So when your classmate stops talking, you can jump in and ask another question! But remember, you have to be a good listener before you can ask good questions.

Last, don't forget to share! Tell your classmates something interesting about yourself. Then your new friends can get to know you too! Soon enough, you'll be the best of friends!

title: Nwa
text:
Once upon a time, the world was very young and there were no people on the earth. One day, the goddess Nwa sat by the river. After washing her face and tidying her hair, she decided to make something special. She took some clay from the river bank and made a tiny figure like herself. She put the clay figure on the ground and gave it life.

The clay figure grew up day by day, but it had no one to play with. Then Nwa made more clay figures: some boys and some girls. They could run, laugh and play with each other. As they grew up, they enjoyed a happy life.

title: Unit 2 · Family Ties in Names
text:
Hello! My name is Alan, and I'm from the UK. Here most people have a first, middle, and last name. My full name is Alan Luke Wood. Alan is my first name, Luke is my middle name, and Wood is my last name. We also call the last name a "family name" or "surname".

My grandfather also has three names. His full name is George Charles Wood. My father's name is the same as my grandfather's. Can you guess why? It shows great respect for my grandfather. People call my father George Charles Wood Junior, and they call my grandfather George Charles Wood Senior.

My mother's name was Linda Grant, but now her name is Linda Wood. Why is that? Because in the UK, a woman often changes her family name to her husband's family name. Sometimes, however, the woman's last name and the man's last name are joined together. This allows both family names to live on.

title: Unit 2 · Mulan
text:
Mulan, the eldest daughter in her family, loved her family very much. When she was young, her dad taught her how to fight and be strong.

One day, the emperor made a rule that every family had to send at least one boy to be in the army. But in Mulan's family, her brother was still a little kid and couldn't go, and her father wasn't healthy.

"What can I do to help?" Mulan thought. "Well, I know! I can fight too. I can go in place of my dad and join the army."

To join the army, Mulan dressed up like a boy. She was brave on the battlefield for a long, long time. No one in the army knew she was a girl.

title: Unit 3 · My Floating School
text:
My name is Sadia Khatun. I'm from Bangladesh. It's difficult to walk on some roads in the rainy season here. So how do I go to school? It's easy! The school comes to me! I study on a "floating school".

My floating school is a "school bus" and classroom all in one. The boat picks me up early in the morning. Our classroom is on the boat too. There are several boats on the river at the same time. Each boat has one teacher and one class. The teacher teaches us all the subjects.

The boat is long and wide. We sit at wooden desks. Big windows bring in lots of sunlight and fresh air. There's a blackboard at the front. There's a computer next to it, and it gets its power from the sun. At the end of the school day, the boat takes me home.

The "floating school" is open in the rainy season. The boat picks students up in the morning. There are two teachers on each boat. Every student on the boat has a computer. Sadia sleeps on the boat at night.

title: Unit 3 · Sima Guang: The Young Hero
text:
During the Song Dynasty, there lived a clever boy named Sima Guang. One sunny day, he was having fun with his friends in a beautiful garden. One boy saw a big water vat. He tried to climb to the top of it, but he didn't know how much water was in it. Suddenly, he lost his balance and fell into the water.

The water inside was deep, and the boy could not swim. He started crying for help.

Just then, Sima Guang found a stone. He got an idea. He picked up the stone and hit the vat. The vat was broken and the water gushed out. The boy was saved and everyone was no longer worried.

title: Unit 4 · Cao Chong: A Smart Boy
text: When Cao Chong was five or six years old, his father, Cao Cao, received a gift—an elephant. Cao Cao wanted to know the elephant's weight, but it wasn't easy to find out. Just then, Cao Chong got a great idea. He said to his father, "Give me a big boat and lots of stones. I can weigh the elephant. First, lead the elephant onto the boat. When the boat starts to sink a bit, draw a line on the side to show the water level. Next, lead the elephant off the boat. Then, put the stones on the boat until the water reaches the line. Finally, weigh the stones. This way, we'll know the elephant's weight."

title: Unit 5 · Alice's Vlog: My Drama Club
text:
This is Mr Ford, our drama teacher. Mr Ford is very nice, and he always has great ideas. He helps me so much!

My parents often come to our shows. They record the shows, and we watch them on TV later. Here's a clip from our last show. That's me with the blonde hair! I look cute, don't I?

The drama club can be hard when I have to remember a lot of lines, but it helps me to understand a lot more about the plays. I am usually very shy, but when I am in a play, I no longer feel afraid. Now I'm brave enough to talk, and even sing, in front of lots of people.

title: Unit 5 · China Enters Space Club
text:
On 24th April 1970, China launched its very first satellite, Dongfanghong-1! China became the fifth country in the world to have its own satellites in space.

People were so excited when they heard the news. They looked up at the night sky to see Dongfanghong-1. The satellite stayed up there for 28 days, and collected lots of important information for scientists to research.

Zhou Zhicheng was just a 7-year-old boy when Dongfanghong-1 was launched. He remembered, "I can hear the song The East Is Red on the radio. When Dongfanghong-1 flew over China, my parents and grandparents were very happy." As he grew older, Zhou Zhicheng followed in the footsteps of those who worked on Dongfanghong-1. He became a scientist and even joined the team which researched Dongfanghong-5.

title: Unit 6 · The World's Longest Rivers
text:
The Yellow River is one of the longest rivers in the world. It's about 5,464 kilometers long and flows into the Bohai Sea. It's the second longest river in China. It is called "Mother River" of China because it brought yellow silt from the mountains, creating fertile land for farming.

The Nile River is the longest river in the world. It has a length of about 6,671 kilometers and enters the Mediterranean Sea. Many people live along the banks of the Nile River. It's also one of the most famous rivers in the world.

The Amazon River is the second longest river in the world. It runs about 6,480 kilometers to the Atlantic Ocean. Its waters feed the world's largest tropical rainforest, which is full of monkeys, birds, and giant fish.

The Yellow River is the longest river in the world. The Yellow River is called "Mother River" of China. The Nile River is thought to be longer than the Amazon River. The Nile River is the second longest river in the world. The Amazon Rainforest is the largest tropical rainforest.

title: Unit 6 · The Grand Canal: A Marvel of China
text:
China has a long history of canals. The people living along these canals are very proud of them. One of the most famous is the Beijing- Hangzhou Canal. It's one of the longest and the oldest canals in the world, and still used. It runs from Beijing to Hangzhou.

It connects five big river systems in China, including the Changjiang River Basin and the Yellow River Basin. For thousands of years, it helped people move food, silk, and other goods. Even now, boats carry things like coal and wood along it. The Grand Canal is like a "living bridge" . It shows how clever and hard-working Chinese people are!
